name: Calydrin
description: Calydrin is a targeted amygdala suppression compound delivered via neural-direct interface, specifically designed to chemically blunt the fear response without impairing threat recognition or rational decision-making. Where berserker compounds flood users with aggression, Calydrin simply removes the emotional static of fear — users remain fully rational and tactically aware but experience no anxiety, no panic, and no instinctive threat-avoidance behavior. Lazarus developed it for high-stakes negotiators and executive protection teams before it became indispensable in combat applications.
effects: Elimination of panic and anxiety under threat
Preservation of full cognitive function and tactical reasoning
Steadied fine motor control under fire
Reduced physiological stress response (controlled heart rate, steady hands)
Emotional flatness across negative emotion spectrum
side_effects: Suppression extends to all negative emotions, including appropriate caution
Users frequently take risks they would otherwise correctly identify as suicidal
Extended use causes persistent emotional blunting between doses
Reported cases of users developing long-term inability to feel fear naturally
Neural-direct delivery carries interface infection risk
cultural_context: Calydrin is the combat drug of choice for professionals who need to think clearly under fire — it is the stimulant that corporate operators, high-end fixers, and Tier 4 security consultants use rather than the blunt instruments of the Shelf. There is a cultural divide in M88 combat culture between those who take Calydrin (controlled, professional, expensive) and those who take Vorrathine (cheap, chaotic, desperate). The drug's emotional blunting side effect has created a small but notable population of ex-military users who find they can no longer feel much of anything.
story_hooks: A Lazarus executive has been on Calydrin continuously for six months — she is running the company with eerie precision but her colleagues are beginning to realize she cannot be reasoned with emotionally, making her unpredictable in a different way.
A runner who uses Calydrin regularly realizes during a quiet moment that she has not felt genuine fear in over a year — and that this might mean she can no longer recognize when she should run.

Someone is distributing Calydrin without prescriptions in Tier 2, targeting workers in dangerous industrial jobs — the supplier has a humanitarian justification, but the funding trail goes somewhere darker.
